citation.title: Experimental Study of the Ion Critical-Gradient Length and Stiffness Level and the Impact of Rotation in the JET Tokamak
citation.authors: P. Mantica, D. Strintzi, T. Tala, C. Giroud, T. Johnson, H. Leggate, E. Lerche, T. Loarer, A. G. Peeters, A. Salmi, S. Sharapov, D. Van Eester, P. C. de Vries, L. Zabeo, K.-D. Zastrow

topic: Ion temperature gradient (ITG) threshold and Ti-profile stiffness in JET core; effect of toroidal rotation
own_question: What are the critical R/LTi and the stiffness level at rho_tor of about 0.33, and how does rotation change them?
actual_method_and_evidence: Offline steady-state scans of ICRH and NBI power in L-mode at JET. Ti came from charge-exchange (CX) spectroscopy, fitted exponentially over 5 channels and time-averaged. qi was gyro-Bohm normalized. The authors also used ICRH Ti modulation analysed with ASTRA/CGM fits, co- versus counter-NBI comparisons, and GS2 linear and nonlinear runs. Reported results: low-rotation threshold of about 3.5±0.3 with high stiffness. Higher rotation gave higher R/LTi, which the authors attribute mainly to reduced stiffness. This attribution relies on assuming the Waltz-rule threshold shift. The study is core, not pedestal, and does not report which impurity species CX measured.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: In JET low-rotation L-mode core plasmas, measured R/LTi stayed near a critical value of about 3.5 despite large changes in normalized ion heat flux. This indicates stiff Ti profiles in that regime.
claim_checks.qualification: Core (rho_tor 0.33), JET only, not the pedestal. Results are offline and steady-state. The source does not specify an impurity versus main-ion distinction for the CX Ti.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Toroidal rotation was associated with higher core R/LTi. The authors interpreted this as reduced stiffness, supported by modulation and co/counter-NBI comparisons.
claim_checks.qualification: This is the authors' interpretation, not a demonstrated mechanism. The threshold at high rotation was not identified.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. The source uses time-averaged stationary CX profiles and does not address nowcasting or report latency.
validation_if_relevant: Consistency checks across experiment types and comparison with gyrokinetic codes. There is no predictive held-out validation.
forbidden_inferences: Pedestal-top CES temperature dynamics follow core stiffness.
Stiffness justifies a specific nowcasting estimator or implies predictability at 10 ms.
Physics findings transfer from JET to KSTAR.
CX Ti here is a carbon impurity measurement.
Rotation causally reduces stiffness as proven physics.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional background for why Ti profiles can be tied to critical gradients, which may motivate partial temporal persistence. It is core-region and offline, so it should not support claims about pedestal nowcasting.
